text:
sarah: Heads-up — planning to lift the runtime pin for runtime v3.2 on the canary cohort during nightshift at 00:30 UTC. Before we unpin I want an explicit rollback/telemetry gate and a short handoff note for whoever's on-call. :eyes:

mike: +1. can we lock down the exact metric queries and thresholds? also confirm whether deploybot will auto-unpin or just run a staged rollout.

carol: We currently have deploybot set to "auto-unpin-on-gates" for this group but we usually turn that off for night windows. Proposal: keep auto-unpin enabled but require BOTH evaluation and infra gates to pass for 10m.

deploybot: Deploybot: current pinlist shows runtime v3.2 pinned since 1715004321. Auto-unpin policy: enabled. I will attempt unpin at scheduled time if gates pass.

ben: For quality/evals gate, require no regression on our smoke promptset (latency ok) and hallucination delta < 1.5% vs baseline. If evals fail, immediate rollback.

tim: For infra gate, suggest these thresholds: p95 latency < 350ms AND error_rate < 0.25% for 10m rolling. If either breaches for 3 consecutive 1m windows, trigger rollback.

mike: PromQL snippets to use (feel free to copy into deploybot gate):
```promql
# p95 generation latency for runtime v3.2
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{runtime="v3.2"}[5m])) by (le))

# 5xx error rate
sum(rate(redwood_runtime_requests_total{runtime="v3.2",code=~"5.."}[5m]))
/ sum(rate(redwood_runtime_requests_total{runtime="v3.2"}[5m]))
```

carol: To keep it simple for nightshift: rollback criteria = ANY of the following:
- infra p95 > 400ms sustained over 5m (:rotating_light:)
- 5xx rate > 0.5% over 5m
- smoke-eval failure (regression or hallucination delta > 2%)
If triggered, deploybot should revert to previous runtime and open a PT.

ben: Add a manual sanity check: if human sees an obvious quality regression but gates still pass, allow manual rollback with `/deploybot rollback runtime=v3.2` and mark reason.

sarah: Handoff plan: @tim will be primary night on-call, @mike secondary. If rollback happens, eskalate to eng-releases and paged oncall. Add note to release notes that this is a canary, may be rolled back automatically.

tim: I'll take night. I'll be online and will monitor the canary dashboard and the smoke eval channel. If I see p95 creeping, I'll call rollback immediately.

mike: Also add a short-lived trace sample check for token dropouts. Quick query: 
```promql
sum(rate(redwood_token_emit_failures_total{runtime="v3.2"}[1m]))
```
If > 5 spikes in 1m, rollback.

deploybot: Acknowledged. Sample deploybot command that will run if gates pass:
```
/unpin runtime=v3.2 --cohort=canary --window=10m --prom-gates-file=/etc/deploy/gates/rt-3.2-canary.yaml
```
The gate file contains the promql thresholds and eval webhook.

carol: Document the rollback runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-unpin-rollback (add to the thread and pin it in the channel).

ben: Small note for release notes: mention potential p95 variability for short period and that we've got auto-rollback guards. Keeps customer support prepped.

sarah: Final checklist for 00:30 UTC:
- Deploybot gates file reviewed (mike)
- Smoke eval webhook enabled (ben)
- On-call assigned (tim primary, mike secondary)
- Runbook link posted (carol)
If everybody is good I'll flip the schedule on deploybot to attempt the unpin at 00:30 UTC.

mike: Gates file updated and pushed to /deploy-configs. I also added the tenant-level exclusion for high-volume partners to avoid noisy signals during warmups.

carol: Runbook link posted and pinned in the channel.

ben: Eval webhook enabled and smoke set queued.

tim: I'm on-call and will watch. Good to go from me.

sarah: OK — setting deploybot to run at 00:30 UTC and will monitor for first 20m post-unpin. If no alarms, we widen cohort at 01:00 UTC.

deploybot: Scheduled: /unpin runtime=v3.2 cohort=canary at 1728601800 (00:30 UTC). I will post status updates in this thread when I start and after gates evaluate.

sarah: Thanks team. If anything changes ping here or page. :thumbsup:
